pages.api:
# API

> A status object, then an optional SenML pack. The HTTP export is GET-only and bound to 127.0.0.1:8057.

## Stdout

Line 1 is always one JSON object:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `schema` | `weavelogic.cog-output.v0` |
| `health` | `ok`, `degraded`, or `no_source` |
| `timestamp` | Unix seconds |
| `error` | `null`, or why a quantity or the sample is missing |
| `source.bus` | `/dev/i2c-1` unless you set another bus |
| `source.address` | `0x76` or `0x77` |
| `source.source_id` | The `--source-id` string, default `bme680/` |
| `source.simulated` | `true` only for `--simulate` |
| `source.verified` | Always `false` until hardware is measured |
| `temperature_c`, `humidity_rh`, `pressure_pa`, `gas_ohm` | Numbers, or `null`. Never a stand-in zero. |

Line 2, only when at least one quantity exists and `--readings-out` is not set, is a SenML pack: a JSON array.

| Record | `n` | `u` |
|---|---|---|
| Temperature | `temperature` | `Cel` |
| Humidity | `humidity` | `%RH` |
| Pressure | `pressure` | `Pa` |
| Gas resistance | `gas_resistance` | `Ohm` |

`bn` on the first record is `--source-id` and ends with `/`. `proof_` is on every record (`MEASURED` or `SYNTHETIC`) because it does not propagate. `t` is Unix seconds on every record. There is no `bt` and no `bu`. A missing quantity is left out of the array.

`gas_resistance` is not in the short example vocabulary in RuView ADR-384. Unknown names are stored and counted. They are not people, tracks, or bounding boxes.

`--readings-out PATH` writes that array to the file instead of stdout. The status line is still printed. A failed sample does not create the file and does not write zeros.

## HTTP

Bound to `127.0.0.1:8057` unless `--api-bind` sets another port on `127.0.0.1`. Other hosts are refused.

| Method and path | Body |
|---|---|
| `GET /` | A short index |
| `GET /status` | The latest status object |
| `GET /readings` | The latest SenML array, or a JSON object with `"readings": null` when there is no pack |
| `GET /guide` | `{"toml", "pages"}` for this cog version |

`GET /readings` is never `[]`. An empty array would look like a successful pack with no records.

The cog does not implement `PUT`. If the Seed's app API accepts `PUT /api/v1/apps/bme680/config`, that call replaces the whole config. Send every key.

There is no store vector. These four numbers are not an embedding, and they are not ingested as one.

## Flags

`--once`, `--simulate`, `--interval`, `--i2c-bus`, `--i2c-addr`, `--device`, `--source-id`, `--heater-c`, `--heat-ms`, `--api-bind`, `--readings-out`, `--help`.

An unknown flag, including `--spatial-out`, exits 2 with empty stdout. This binary has no spatial-evidence feature.
pages.calibrate:
# Calibrate

> There is no user calibration. The chip's own coefficients are read, not written. This cog does not produce an air-quality index.

The BME680 stores temperature, pressure, humidity and heater coefficients in its registers. The cog reads them and applies the datasheet's floating-point compensation. It never writes those registers, and it never writes the soft-reset register.

## What you can set

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--heater-c` | 300 | Hot-plate target in °C, written as `res_heat_0`. Datasheet range used here is 200 to 400. |
| `--heat-ms` | 100 | How long the plate stays hot, written as `gas_wait_0`. The datasheet's 100 ms example is the byte `0x59`. |
| `--source-id` | `bme680/` | The SenML base name. This is the installed board's object id. It must end with `/`. It is not the catalog type `bme680-breakout`. |

The first sample's heater code uses a hardcoded ambient temperature of 25 °C, which the datasheet allows. Later samples use the previous compensated temperature when it was inside −40 °C to 85 °C. That ambient value is not itself a published reading.

Oversampling is fixed at the datasheet quick start: humidity ×1, temperature ×2, pressure ×16. The IIR filter is left off (the reset state), so one sample is not smeared with an older one.

## What you do not get

Bosch's BSEC software computes IAQ, a static IAQ, a CO2 equivalent and a breath-VOC equivalent, and it tracks accuracy and run-in. BSEC is closed source and is not in this cog. Those names are not in the SenML pack. Do not treat gas resistance as an IAQ score. A higher resistance is not "better air" unless you have established that for this board and this heater profile. That has not been measured here.

If `heat_stab_r` is clear, the gas record is omitted and the status is `degraded`. The cog does not fill the gap with zero ohms. Lengthen `--heat-ms` or lower `--heater-c` only after you have a reason to; both are untested on this board.
pages.glossary:
# Glossary

> Names used in this cog, with the meaning this guide actually uses.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| SenML | RFC 8428 sensor markup. This cog writes one JSON array (a pack) per sample. |
| `bn` | Base name. The installed board's object id, default `bme680/`. It must end with `/` so it does not glue onto `temperature`. |
| `proof_` | On every record. `MEASURED` for a real I2C sample, `SYNTHETIC` for `--simulate`. It does not carry from the first record to the next. `CODE` is not used. |
| `Cel` | SenML unit for degrees Celsius. Not `C` and not `degC`. |
| `%RH` | SenML unit for relative humidity. |
| `Pa` | Pascal. 100 Pa is 1 hPa. The cog does not convert to hPa. |
| `Ohm` | Ohm, the gas-sensor resistance after compensation. |
| Forced mode | One temperature, pressure, humidity and gas cycle, then the chip returns to sleep. |
| `no_source` | The sample did not happen. Values are null. |
| `degraded` | The chip answered, but at least one quantity is missing. |
| CSB | Chip-select. Tie it to VDDIO or the part selects SPI and ignores I2C until power is removed. |
| SDO | Address strap. Low is 0x76, high is 0x77. Not a Pi GPIO in this wiring. |
| Chip id | Register 0xD0. The datasheet's reset value is 0x61. |
| BSEC | Bosch's closed-source library for IAQ and related indexes. Not linked into this cog. |
| Object reading | The state of a thing (this board's air). Not evidence that a person is present. |
| `spatial.evidence.v1` | The perception-evidence line this cog does not emit. |
pages.parts:
# Parts

> Purple BME680 breakout, four jumper wires, and a Cognitum Seed. The chip mark is the identification this cog relies on.

| Part | Role |
|---|---|
| Breakout with a chip marked BME680 | The sensor. Purple PCB in the owner's notes. This lane did not inspect that photo. |
| Four jumper wires | 3.3 V, ground, SDA, SCL |
| Cognitum Seed | Pi Zero 2 W header, I2C bus 1 (`/dev/i2c-1`) |

## What this lane could not see

The task describes a purple breakout and a chip marked BME680. The album photo was not available here, so none of the following were read off the board:

- Whether a regulator sits between the header VCC and the chip, or the header is the chip's raw VDD (1.71 V to 3.6 V)
- The silkscreen names (VCC versus VDD, SDA versus SDI, and so on)
- Whether SDO is strapped to ground (address 0x76) or to VDDIO (address 0x77)
- Whether CSB is tied to VDDIO. If it is not high at power-up, the chip locks into SPI until the breakout itself loses power.

Trust the labels printed on your board over the datasheet nicknames in **Wiring**, and over wire colours.

## Look-alikes

The BME280 is temperature, pressure and humidity only: no gas, and a different chip id. The BME688 is a later gas sensor. Bosch's BME68x API uses chip id 0x61 for both the BME680 and the BME688. This datasheet does not define a register that separates them. The cog checks for 0x61 and then speaks the BME680 forced-mode sequence. It does not implement BME688 scan mode. If the chip is not marked BME680, do not assume these numbers.

A BMP280 or BMP388 is pressure (and sometimes temperature) only and will not answer as chip id 0x61. The cog refuses any other id and does not invent a sample.
pages.safety:
# Safety

> Not a safety device, not a gas alarm, and not a medical sensor. 3.3 V only.

The BME680's gas output is a resistance that moves when many volatile compounds are present. It does not tell you whether a room is safe to enter, whether a heater is leaking a specific gas, or what the carbon dioxide concentration is. Do not use this cog to permit or deny occupancy, ventilation shutdown, or breathing decisions.

Bosch documents an internal hot plate, typically 200 °C to 400 °C, under the metal lid. This cog's default target is 300 °C for 100 ms. That temperature is inside the package. It is not a reason to run the board from 5 V, and it is not a surface you should treat as a heater you can touch for warmth. Follow the datasheet's absolute maximums: supply pins −0.3 V to 4.25 V.

The Pi header's 5 V pins (pin 2 and pin 4) must not feed this breakout until someone has confirmed a regulator on this purple board. This lane could not see one. The GPIO pins are not 5 V tolerant. A 5 V I2C pull-up on the breakout is the same hazard.

The export listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Gas resistance and humidity are still information about the place the Seed sits. Do not republish the export onto a LAN from this cog; it will refuse a non-loopback bind.

No claim here has been checked on the physical board.
pages.sensor:
# The sensor

> A Bosch Sensortec BME680: gas, pressure, humidity and temperature in one 3.0 mm package, read over I2C.

The BME680 measures four quantities and then sleeps. Gas resistance is the resistance of a metal-oxide layer after the internal hot plate has been held at a target temperature (this cog's default is the datasheet quick start: 300 °C for 100 ms). It responds to many volatile compounds. It is not selective for one gas, and it is not a CO2 sensor.

## Good for

- Temperature, relative humidity and barometric pressure at the board
- A raw gas-resistance trend, in ohms, for the same board over time

## Not for

- Deciding whether air is safe to breathe
- Counting people, tracking them, or drawing a box around them
- Indoor-air-quality index, CO2-equivalent or breath-VOC. Those are BSEC outputs. This cog does not compute them.
- 5 V power or 5 V I2C pull-ups

## Datasheet spec (vendor, not our measurement)

Source: Bosch Sensortec BST-BME680-DS001-09, document revision 1.9, February 2024.

| Item | Vendor figure |
|---|---|
| Supply VDD | 1.71 V to 3.6 V |
| I/O VDDIO | 1.2 V to 3.6 V |
| Absolute maximum on VDD or VDDIO | −0.3 V to 4.25 V |
| Operating temperature, full accuracy | −40 °C to 85 °C |
| Humidity | 0 %RH to 100 %RH |
| Pressure, full accuracy | 300 hPa to 1100 hPa |
| I2C address | 0x76 (SDO low) or 0x77 (SDO high) |
| Chip id | 0x61 at register 0xD0 |
| Interface | I2C or SPI. This cog speaks I2C only. |

## What a line looks like

With a sample, stdout is a status object and then a SenML array. `proof_` is `MEASURED` on a real sample and `SYNTHETIC` under `--simulate`.

With no device, stdout is one object: `health` is `no_source`, the four values are `null`, and `error` names `/dev/i2c-1` and the address. There is no second line.
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Install the cog, confirm the bus, then take one sample. Simulation does not need the sensor.

## Check the bus

On the Seed, `/dev/i2c-1` should exist. If it does not, I2C is off or a reflash removed it. Turning it on changes boot configuration and needs the owner's approval. This cog will not do that.

`i2cdetect` is not assumed to be installed. The cog's own `no_source` line and `GET /status` are the probe.

## Sideload

Cross-build and sideload are done by the seed operator, with approval, because they write onto the Seed:

```text
scripts/cross-build.sh bme680
scripts/seed-sideload.sh bme680 genesis@<seed>
```

`<seed>` is the device's name. Do not put a LAN or tailnet address in this guide.

## Simulate, then one real sample

On a machine without the sensor, or from the Seed console:

```text
cog-bme680 --once --simulate
```

Expect two lines. The status object has `"simulated": true` and `"health": "ok"`. The second line is a JSON array whose every record has `"proof_": "SYNTHETIC"`. The numbers are the compensation of a fixed fake calibration image. They are not the air in the room.

With the breakout wired:

```text
cog-bme680 --once
```

A real sample has `"proof_": "MEASURED"` and `"simulated": false`. `"verified": false` stays false until someone has compared the cog with a reference instrument on this hardware. That has not happened yet.

If the board is missing, the command still exits 0 and prints one line: `"health": "no_source"`, four nulls, and an `error` that names the bus and the address. No SenML line.

## Run continuously

```text
cog-bme680 --interval 10
```

Each interval is one forced-mode measurement. The export at `http://127.0.0.1:8057` on the Seed is up before the sensor is opened, so a missing board is visible at `/status` instead of a refused connection.

The console may run only the commands listed in `cog.toml`: `--help`, `--once`, and `--once --simulate`.
pages.start:
# Start here

> Read temperature, humidity, pressure and gas resistance from a Bosch BME680 on a Cognitum Seed. The numbers describe the board's air, not a person.

The `bme680` cog takes one forced-mode sample over I2C and prints a status line plus a SenML pack (RFC 8428). Temperature is in `Cel`, humidity in `%RH`, pressure in `Pa`, and gas resistance in `Ohm`. It does not emit `spatial.evidence.v1`, a track, or a bounding box. ADR-107 has no record type for these quantities.

Hardware is not yet tested. `--simulate` runs the real compensation math on a fixed synthetic calibration image and labels the pack `SYNTHETIC`. That proves the cog, not the sensor.

## The 5-minute path

1. **Identify the board.** A purple breakout whose chip is marked BME680. → see **Parts**
2. **Wire 3.3 V, ground, SDA and SCL.** Do not use 5 V. Strap CSB and SDO on the breakout. → see **Wiring**
3. **Confirm I2C is enabled** on the Seed (`/dev/i2c-1`). Enabling it is an owner approval. This cog does not edit boot files. → see **Set up**
4. **Try the software with no sensor:** `cog-bme680 --once --simulate`. → see **Set up**
5. **One real sample:** `cog-bme680 --once`. A missing board prints one `no_source` line and exits 0. It does not print zeros. → see **Troubleshoot**

## How the data flows

```diagram
flow
```

The part wakes, measures temperature, pressure and humidity, heats the gas sensor, measures its resistance, and returns to sleep. The cog compensates the raw ADC values with the calibration bytes stored on the chip.

## What you get

| Output | Where | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Status object | stdout, one JSON object | `health` of `ok`, `degraded` or `no_source`. Missing quantities are `null`. |
| SenML pack | the next stdout line, or `--readings-out` | One JSON array. Object readings, not people. |
| Export | `http://127.0.0.1:8057` on the Seed | `GET /status`, `GET /readings`, `GET /guide` |

→ see **API** for every field.

## Honest limits

- **Not yet tested** on a Seed or on this breakout. No measured error against a reference thermometer, hygrometer or barometer.
- **Not an air-quality index.** Bosch's IAQ, CO2-equivalent and breath-VOC figures come from the closed-source BSEC library. This cog does not run BSEC and does not invent those numbers.
- **Not presence.** A temperature is the state of this object. It does not mean a person is here.
- **The purple board's power path was not visible** to this lane (regulator versus the chip's raw 1.71–3.6 V pin). Treat the header as 3.3 V only.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> A missing sensor is `no_source` with nulls. A partial sample is `degraded`. Neither one is a row of zeros.

| Health | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ok` | Temperature, humidity, pressure and gas resistance are all present. |
| `degraded` | The chip answered, but at least one quantity is missing. `error` says which. |
| `no_source` | The bus did not yield a sample. All four values are `null`. Exit code is still 0 for `--once`. |

## Nothing answered at 0x76 on /dev/i2c-1

The error text names the address and the bus, and it names the next physical check. Work down this list.

1. **Wrong bus or port.** The header is `/dev/i2c-1` (`--i2c-bus 1`). A UART cog's `/dev/serial0` is a different problem; this part is not on the serial console.
2. **`/dev/i2c-1` does not exist.** I2C is off, or an OTA or reflash turned it off. Enabling `dtparam=i2c_arm=on` and `i2c-dev` needs the owner's approval. This cog does not edit boot files. Check again after every reflash.
3. **Address.** Default `--i2c-addr 0x76` (SDO strapped to GND). Use `0x77` only when SDO is strapped to VDDIO. Any other address is refused (exit 2) and prints nothing on stdout.
4. **CSB.** CSB must be at VDDIO while the breakout powers up, or the chip locks into SPI and will not answer I2C. This lane could not see that strap on the purple board.
5. **Power-cycle the breakout.** A Seed reboot leaves the 3.3 V pin up, so the sensor does not reset. Unplug the breakout's VDD, or remove power from the Seed entirely.
6. **3.3 V and ground.** Pin 1 and pin 6. Not the 5 V pins.
7. **Another cog** may be using the same bus. Stop it and retry. I2C is shared; this cog does not lock the bus beyond its own sample.
8. **`i2cdetect`** may not be installed. Use this cog's error line and `GET /status` instead.

Chip id other than 0x61 is also `no_source`. The cog will not compensate a different part and call it a BME680.

## Measurement did not finish, or new_data_0 is clear

The cog waited for the `measuring` bit to clear and then required `new_data_0`. If that does not happen, it does not publish the previous contents of the data registers. Power-cycle the breakout. If it keeps happening, the heater time plus the oversampling wait may be too short for a damaged part; that has not been seen on hardware because the part has not been run.

## Gas is null but temperature is present

`gas_valid_r` or `heat_stab_r` was clear, or the heater code could not be computed. The status is `degraded` and the SenML pack has no `gas_resistance` record. That is a failed gas conversion, not zero ohms. The datasheet says a clear `heat_stab_r` means the heat time was too short or the target was too high.

## Quick isolation

1. `--once --simulate` prints a `SYNTHETIC` pack. If that fails, the cog binary is the problem.
2. `--once` with the breakout unplugged prints one `no_source` line. If it prints numbers, something else is answering at that address.
3. `--once` with the breakout powered. Still untested on this hardware.

## Last resorts

- Exit 2 and empty stdout means a refused argument (`--device` outside `/dev`, a bad address, `--api-bind` not on `127.0.0.1`, an unknown flag). Fix the command. The sensor was not opened.
- A `PUT` of the Seed app config replaces every key. Send the whole config, not one field.
- Do not point this cog at a UART device and expect frames. It speaks I2C register reads only.
pages.wiring:
# Wiring

> 3.3 V logic only. Four wires to the Seed header, plus two straps that stay on the breakout.

```diagram
header
```

```diagram
wiring
```

The diagram uses the datasheet pin names, not a silkscreen this lane has read. If your board says VCC, SDA and SCL, those are the same nets as VDD, SDI and SCK. Trust the board's labels.

| Breakout | Seed header | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| VDD (board label may say VCC) | Pin 1, 3V3 | Not pin 2 or pin 4. See below. |
| GND | Pin 6, GND | Common ground |
| SDI (board label may say SDA) | Pin 3, GPIO2, SDA | I2C data |
| SCK (board label may say SCL) | Pin 5, GPIO3, SCL | I2C clock |
| SDO | Strap on the breakout | GND → address 0x76 (the default). VDDIO → 0x77. Do not leave it floating. |
| CSB | Strap to VDDIO (3.3 V) | Selects I2C. If CSB is low at power-up, the chip locks into SPI until the breakout's power is removed. |

SDO and CSB are not wired to Pi GPIO. They are straps on the breakout. This lane could not see how the purple board straps them.

## 3.3 V, not 5 V

Datasheet (vendor, not our measurement): VDD is 1.71 V to 3.6 V, VDDIO is 1.2 V to 3.6 V, and the absolute maximum on either supply pin is 4.25 V. Interface pins must stay within −0.3 V to VDDIO + 0.3 V. The Pi's GPIO is not 5 V tolerant. A 5 V header pin, or a breakout whose I2C pull-ups go to 5 V, can damage the Pi even if the sensor survives.

**Unverified:** whether this purple board has a regulator between the header and the chip. Until that is seen, power it only from pin 1 (3.3 V).

## Power-cycle the breakout, not just the Seed

A Seed reboot does not drop the 3.3 V pin, so the BME680 stays powered. Changing the SDO strap or repairing a CSB that was low at power-up does nothing until the breakout itself loses power. Unplug the breakout's VDD wire, or unplug the Seed's supply. Then plug it back.

I2C on the Seed (`dtparam=i2c_arm=on` and the `i2c-dev` module) is an owner approval. This cog does not edit `/boot`. If a reflash or OTA removes `/dev/i2c-1`, the cog reports that the open failed; it does not turn the bus back on.
